title: बालेनको भारत भ्रमणले लज्जित बनाएको एमाले महासचिवको टिप्पणी
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । नेकपा (एमाले) का महासचिव शंकर पोखरेलले प्रधानमन्त्रीको हालैको भारत भ्रमण नेपालको राष्ट्रिय हित र सरोकारका विषयमा अपेक्षाअनुसार उपलब्धिमूलक हुन नसकेको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्। प्रेस चौतारी कास्कीले आयोजना गरेको पत्रकार भेटघाट कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै प्रधानमन्त्रीको भारत भ्रमणले नेपालको राष्ट्रिय स्वाभिमान, सीमा विवाद र राष्ट्रिय हितका विषयमा ठोस उपलब्धि दिन नसकेको बताए। प्रधानमन्त्रीको भारत भ्रमणले देशलाई लज्जित बनाएको टिप्पणी गरे। विगतमा राष्ट्रियताको विषयमा चर्को अभिव्यक्ति दिने प्रधानमन्त्रीले भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा नेपालको सीमा विवादबारे समेत प्रभावकारी रूपमा कुरा उठाउन नसकेको आरोप लगाए। उनले भने, ‘प्रधानमन्त्रीको भारत भ्रमणले हामी सबैलाई लज्जित बनाएको छ। काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाको कार्यालयमा ग्रेटर नेपालको नक्सा राखेर नेताहरू माथि व्यङ्ग्य गर्नुहुन्थ्यो। हरेक भ्रमणमा उहाँले अर्ती उपदेश दिनुहुन्थ्यो। अस्ति उहाँ भारत भ्रमणमा जानुभयो। नेपालका हित र सरोकारका विषयमा केही कुरा राख्न सक्नुभएन।’ लिपुलेक, लिम्पियाधुरा र कालापानीलगायत सीमा विवादका विषयमा छलफल नै नभएको र भारतीय विदेश मन्त्रालयका प्रवक्ताले समेत ती विषय भ्रमणको एजेन्डामा नरहेको बताएको बताए। नेपाल–भारत सम्बन्धको पुनरावलोकनका लागि एमाले नेतृत्वको सरकारका समयमा गठन भएको प्रबुद्ध व्यक्ति समूह (ईपीजी) को प्रतिवेदनसमेत भारतले बुझ्न नमानेको अवस्थामा प्रधानमन्त्रीले त्यसलाई स्वीकार गर्न र कार्यान्वयनमा लैजान आग्रह गर्न नसकेको बताए। पोखरा र भैरहवा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलसँग जोडिएको हवाई रुटको विषयमा पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीको भारत भ्रमणबाट ठोस सहमति हुन नसकेको बताए। उनले भने, ‘हिजो हवाई रुट नदिएर अड्किएको थियो, आज उडानको उचाइ कति हुने भन्ने बहसका नाममा नेपालले प्रयोग गर्न नपाउने स्थिति उत्पन्न हुन सक्छ।’ भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा दुई खर्ब रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी ऋण प्राप्त गर्नुलाई उपलब्धिका रूपमा प्रचार गरिएकोप्रति पनि प्रश्न उठाए। विगतमा ऋणले देश डुबाएको भन्दै आलोचना गर्ने राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीका नेताहरू अहिले ऋण प्राप्तिलाई उपलब्धि भन्न थालेको टिप्पणी गरे। Kathmandu. CPN (UML) General Secretary Shankar Pokharel has commented that the Prime Minister's recent visit to India has not been as productive as expected in terms of Nepal's national interests and concerns. Speaking at a press meet organized by Press Chautari Kaski, he said that the Prime Minister's visit to India has not yielded any concrete results in Nepal's national pride, border disputes and national interests. He commented that the Prime Minister's visit to India has embarrassed the country. He accused the Prime Minister, who has made strong statements on nationalism in the past, of not being able to effectively raise the issue of Nepal's border dispute during his visit to India. He said, 'The Prime Minister's visit to India has embarrassed us all. He used to mock leaders by placing a map of Greater Nepal in the Kathmandu Metropolitan City office. He used to give sermons on every visit. He went on a visit to India yesterday. He could not say anything about the interests and concerns of Nepal.' There was no discussion on border disputes including Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani, and even a spokesperson for the Indian Ministry of External Affairs said that these issues were not on the agenda of the visit. The Prime Minister said that India has not been able to accept and implement the report of the Eminent Persons Group (EPG), formed during the UML-led government to review Nepal-India relations, even though India has refused to understand it. He said that the Prime Minister's visit to India also failed to reach a concrete agreement on the issue of air routes connecting Pokhara and Bhairahawa International Airports. He said, "Yesterday, there was a stalemate over the air route, and today, in the name of debating the altitude of the flight, a situation may arise in which Nepal will not be able to use it." He also questioned the promotion of obtaining a loan of more than 200 billion rupees as an achievement during his visit to India. Leaders of the National Independent Party, who had criticized the country for sinking due to debt in the past, commented that now they are calling obtaining a loan an achievement.

CPN (UML) General Secretary Shankar Pokharel has commented that the Prime Minister's recent visit to India has not been as productive as expected in terms of Nepal's national interests and concerns. Speaking at a press meet organized by Press Chautari Kaski, he said that the Prime Minister's visit to India has not yielded any concrete results in Nepal's national pride, border disputes and national interests. He commented that the Prime Minister's visit to India has embarrassed the country. He accused the Prime Minister, who has made strong statements on nationalism in the past, of not being able to effectively raise the issue of Nepal's border dispute during his visit to India. He said, 'The Prime Minister's visit to India has embarrassed us all. He used to mock leaders by placing a map of Greater Nepal in the Kathmandu Metropolitan City office. He used to give sermons on every visit. He went on a visit to India yesterday. He could not say anything about the interests and concerns of Nepal.' He said that the Prime Minister's visit to India also failed to reach a concrete agreement on the issue of air routes connecting Pokhara and Bhairahawa International Airports. He said, "Yesterday, there was a stalemate over the air route, and today, in the name of debating the altitude of the flight, a situation may arise in which Nepal will not be able to use it." He also questioned the promotion of obtaining a loan of more than 200 billion rupees as an achievement during his visit to India. Leaders of the National Independent Party, who had criticized the country for sinking due to debt in the past, commented that now they are calling obtaining a loan an achievement.

नेपाल–भारत सम्बन्धको पुनरावलोकनका लागि एमाले नेतृत्वको सरकारका समयमा गठन भएको प्रबुद्ध व्यक्ति समूह (ईपीजी) को प्रतिवेदनसमेत भारतले बुझ्न नमानेको अवस्थामा प्रधानमन्त्रीले त्यसलाई स्वीकार गर्न र कार्यान्वयनमा लैजान आग्रह गर्न नसकेको बताए।

पोखरा र भैरहवा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थलसँग जोडिएको हवाई रुटको विषयमा पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीको भारत भ्रमणबाट ठोस सहमति हुन नसकेको बताए।

उनले भने, ‘हिजो हवाई रुट नदिएर अड्किएको थियो, आज उडानको उचाइ कति हुने भन्ने बहसका नाममा नेपालले प्रयोग गर्न नपाउने स्थिति उत्पन्न हुन सक्छ।’

भारत भ्रमणका क्रममा दुई खर्ब रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी ऋण प्राप्त गर्नुलाई उपलब्धिका रूपमा प्रचार गरिएकोप्रति पनि प्रश्न उठाए। विगतमा ऋणले देश डुबाएको भन्दै आलोचना गर्ने राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीका नेताहरू अहिले ऋण प्राप्तिलाई उपलब्धि भन्न थालेको टिप्पणी गरे।

Kathmandu. CPN (UML) General Secretary Shankar Pokharel has commented that the Prime Minister's recent visit to India has not been as productive as expected in terms of Nepal's national interests and concerns. Speaking at a press meet organized by Press Chautari Kaski, he said that the Prime Minister's visit to India has not yielded any concrete results in Nepal's national pride, border disputes and national interests. He commented that the Prime Minister's visit to India has embarrassed the country. He accused the Prime Minister, who has made strong statements on nationalism in the past, of not being able to effectively raise the issue of Nepal's border dispute during his visit to India. He said, 'The Prime Minister's visit to India has embarrassed us all. He used to mock leaders by placing a map of Greater Nepal in the Kathmandu Metropolitan City office. He used to give sermons on every visit. He went on a visit to India yesterday. He could not say anything about the interests and concerns of Nepal.' There was no discussion on border disputes including Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani, and even a spokesperson for the Indian Ministry of External Affairs said that these issues were not on the agenda of the visit. The Prime Minister said that India has not been able to accept and implement the report of the Eminent Persons Group (EPG), formed during the UML-led government to review Nepal-India relations, even though India has refused to understand it. He said that the Prime Minister's visit to India also failed to reach a concrete agreement on the issue of air routes connecting Pokhara and Bhairahawa International Airports. He said, "Yesterday, there was a stalemate over the air route, and today, in the name of debating the altitude of the flight, a situation may arise in which Nepal will not be able to use it." He also questioned the promotion of obtaining a loan of more than 200 billion rupees as an achievement during his visit to India. Leaders of the National Independent Party, who had criticized the country for sinking due to debt in the past, commented that now they are calling obtaining a loan an achievement.
